old:
Four eight-output groups per prompt do not supply 32 independently seeded
responses. Parent seeds increase by one between groups, and the vLLM V0
sampler sets each output's seed to the parent seed plus its zero-based index. The four
ranges therefore contain eleven distinct nominal stream identifiers. For
each prompt and checkpoint, the estimator uses the earliest draw/output
position for each identifier, selected independently of correctness and
key identity. Outputs sharing an identifier sometimes differ, so equal seed
integers do not imply identical outputs. The seed mapping assumes that the
vLLM V0 rule applies across runs; the exact runtime version is not
established for every run.

Two sensitivity comparisons use disjoint stream identifiers across
conditions. Split~0 assigns the lower five identifiers to condition~A and
the upper six to~B; split~1 reverses the assignment. The identifiers are
disjoint within every prompt in both splits across all 627 paired
seed-level comparisons. Each split has its own eligible prompts and
number of defined seeds. The two splits agree with the primary contrast's
direction in eleven of the twelve \texttt{Graph}/\texttt{PantryPlan} Dr.GRPO/GRPO
before/after comparisons and all six Re:Dr-minus-Dr.GRPO comparisons.

Disjoint identifiers do not establish independent draws. Identifiers also
repeat across prompts, so neither the splits nor the jointly eligible
prompt means imply independent prompt observations. Independent sampling
from a fixed policy remains an assumption of the estimator identity.
Comparisons under shared streams are descriptive where joint-selection
assumptions do not hold.

The original \texttt{mean@8}, \texttt{pass@8}, and \texttt{distinct@8} average
the four intact groups. Stream overlap affects dependence, but not the
linearity of these marginal averages. Additional sensitivity comparisons
use individual intact groups, the first group alone, prompt intersections
fixed across seeds, and four-condition change differences. Pooling all
32 positions repeats stream identifiers and serves only as an overlap
diagnostic. These comparisons share outputs and are not independent
replications; missing conditions remain unavailable.
new:
The four eight-output groups overlap in their sampling streams. Under the
vLLM V0 seed convention, they contain eleven distinct nominal stream
identifiers; the concentration estimator uses one representative per
identifier, chosen independently of correctness and key identity. This
mapping is an assumption of the seed-based analysis. Equal identifiers can
produce different outputs, and distinct identifiers do not establish
independent draws.

Two sensitivity comparisons assign disjoint sets of five and six stream
identifiers to the two conditions. Split~0 assigns the lower five to~A and
the upper six to~B; split~1 reverses them. Eligibility is determined
separately for each split. Streams also repeat across prompts, so the
splits do not establish independence across prompts or conditions.
Comparisons remain descriptive where the estimator's independent-sampling
or joint-selection assumptions do not hold.

The original \texttt{mean@8}, \texttt{pass@8}, and \texttt{distinct@8} average
the four intact groups. Stream overlap affects dependence, but not the
linearity of these marginal averages.
